requirements.text: The expanded left sidebar shows two tabs, Projects and Files, and only the selected tab's content is visible: Projects shows the existing Home row and each app with its terminals; Files shows only the file explorer, filling the sidebar's available height. The sidebar opens on Projects when no tab has been chosen.
tests: R1: the expanded sidebar opens on Projects, showing the Home row and apps but not the explorer
R1: choosing Files shows only the explorer, filling the sidebar, and hides the Projects content
R1: clicking a tab never selects an app, a terminal or Home
R1: the chosen tab is not remembered, so reopening starts on Projects again
A1: it is not mounted while Projects is shown, and stays mounted once opened
A2: Projects still lists the Home row, every app and every terminal with a roll-up dot
R1: the explorer sits in the Files tab, not below the last app in Projects
A2: with no explorer prop the Projects content is exactly as before
R1: with no apps saved the sidebar still shows both tabs when the explorer has a folder
A2: expanded keeps the Home row and app rows beside the new Projects | Files strip
A1: starting on Projects reads no folder, Files lists once, and coming back keeps it
R1: the expanded sidebar still lists the Home row, every app and terminal with a roll-up dot
R1: the collapsed rail still keeps Expand, Home and the app initials with their dots
R1: it opens on Projects showing the Home row and apps, and Files shows only the explorer
R1: with no apps but a folder to show, both tabs are there and Files shows the explorer
R1: with no apps and no folder to root at, the sidebar stays hidden as it is today
R1: switching tabs leaves the selected app and its terminals alone
R1: switching tabs never changes the active editor file, its tab or its text

requirements.text: The Projects | Files tab strip stays fixed at the top of the expanded sidebar and remains visible and clickable without vertical scrolling, however many apps and terminals the Projects list contains.
tests: R2: the strip sits outside the scrolling Projects panel, so it cannot scroll away
R2: switching tabs does not reconcile the 500-row Projects list
R2: CSS keeps the strip in a fixed row and lets only the panels scroll
R2: the two tabs stay inside the narrow sidebar without widening it

requirements.text: The collapsed sidebar rail keeps Expand, Home and the app initials with their status dots, and adds a Projects icon and a Files icon. Clicking the Projects icon expands the pane and selects the Projects tab in one action; clicking the Files icon expands the pane and selects the Files tab in one action. The rail's tab icons use the expand/collapse control the sidebar already receives and choose their tab inside the sidebar area, so this revision needs no new tab state or tab handlers in the app shell.
tests: R3: the rail keeps Expand, Home and the app initials and adds the Projects and Files icons
R3: the rail shows both tab icons even with no apps
R3: both rail icons carry an accessible name and a title
R3: clicking the Projects rail icon expands the pane onto Projects in one action
R3: clicking the Files rail icon expands the pane onto Files in one action
R3: the rail visibly marks the active tab
R3: clicking Home or an app initial in the rail does not change the active tab
A2: the collapsed rail keeps Expand, Home and every app initial and now adds the two tab icons
R3: the collapsed rail marks the active tab and leaves the other one inactive
R3: the rail Files and Projects icons expand the pane straight onto their tab
R3: clicking Home or an app initial in the rail keeps today's behaviour and leaves the tab alone

requirements.text: Selecting an app, a terminal, Home or a file never changes the active sidebar tab by itself; in this revision the tab changes only when the user clicks a tab or clicks a rail tab icon.
tests: R4: selecting an app or a terminal in Projects leaves the tab alone
R4: choosing Home from the sidebar does not switch the tab
R4: opening a file from the Files tab leaves the sidebar on Files
R4: in the app view it is the selected app's root and follows a newly selected app
R9: deleting an open file from the explorer closes its tab after one confirmation
R4: choosing Home from the palette does not switch the sidebar tab
R4: selecting an app from the Home screen leaves the sidebar tab alone
R4: a delete that closes an editor tab keeps the sidebar on Files

requirements.text: The tab strip is operable by keyboard and assistive technology: it exposes a tab list with two tabs and a tab panel, marks the selected tab, gives each tab a text label, shows a visible focus, and supports Left/Right arrow keys between the tabs.

R5: it exposes a named tab list with two labelled tabs, a tab panel and the selected tab
R5: Left and Right arrow keys move the selection between the tabs
R5: Enter and Space select the focused tab
R5: the selected tab is announced and also visually distinct, not shown by colour alone
